newsitem.title: USA: USAir mulling options for low-cost service.
newsitem.headline: USAir mulling options for low-cost service.

text.p: USAir Group Inc said Tuesday it was mulling ways to compete against low cost carriers such as Southwest Airlines Co and Delta Air Lines's Express unit.

"We have to compete with the likes of Southwest. We have a need for a low-cost response" or a no-frills product with low employee costs and low distribution expenses, USAir President Rakesh Gangwal said.
The airline declined to comment on what form the low-cost "solution" may take, but management and labor are discussing various possibilities.
USAir and its labor groups also are in talks to reduce operating costs, which remain among the highest in the industry. Labor costs costs comprise about 40 percent of USAir's operating costs.
Wolf said he expect's USAir's low-cost "solution" will affect a larger percentage of the company than seen with Delta Express or the Shuttle by United, part of UAL Corp.
"We don't see it applying to the bulk of the company, but we do see it needing to apply to a substantial part," Wolf said.
USAir must offer service that competes directly with Southwest, which is expanding throughout the east coast, and Delta Express.
"It will happen because the market place dictates that it happen," Wolf said.
"Low cost carrier will grow here (in the east coast). Either we do it or someone else will. And the only way for us to do it is with a cost-competive structure," Gangwal said.
USAir is also examining its contract relationship with its northeast shuttle, which flies from New York to Boston and Washington.
USAir has a six-month window of opportunity to buy the Shuttle, which is owned by creditors of former owner Donald Trump but operated by USAir.
"We fully intend to be associated with the shuttle, to acquire the existing shuttle or start our own," Wolf said.
